{{Short description|American mathematician (b. 1954)}}
'''Michael Loss''' (born 1954)<ref>Birthdate from [https://lccn.loc.gov/n96065238 Library of Congress authority control data]</ref> is a [[mathematician]] and [[mathematical physics|mathematical physicist]] who works as a professor of mathematics at the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]].<ref>[http://www.math.gatech.edu/users/loss Faculty profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160919125650/http://www.math.gatech.edu/users/loss |date=2016-09-19 }}, Georgia Tech., retrieved 2015-01-26.</ref>

Loss obtained his Ph.D. in 1982 from the [[ETH Zurich]], with a dissertation on the [[three-body problem]] jointly supervised by Walter Hunziker and [[Israel Michael Sigal]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=22841}}.</ref>

He coauthors the graduate textbook ''Analysis'' ([[Graduate Studies in Mathematics]] 14. [[American Mathematical Society]], 1997; 2nd ed., 2001) with [[Elliott H. Lieb]].<ref>Review of ''Analysis'' by J. Horváth (1998), {{MR|1415616}}; for the 2nd edition, see {{MR|1817225}}.</ref>

In 2012, he became one of the inaugural [[fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]],<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2015-01-26.</ref> and was elected as a Foreign Corresponding Member of the Chilean Academy of Sciences.<ref>[http://www.math.gatech.edu/news/michael-loss-elected-chilean-academy-sciences Michael Loss elected to Chilean Academy of Sciences] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151011050622/http://www.math.gatech.edu/news/michael-loss-elected-chilean-academy-sciences |date=2015-10-11 }}, Georgia Tech. School of Mathematics, January 18, 2012, retrieved 2015-01-26.</ref> He is one of the 2015 winners of the [[Humboldt Prize]].<ref>[https://www.math.gatech.edu/news/michael-loss-receives-humboldt-research-award Michael Loss Receives the Humboldt Research Award], Georgia Tech. School of Mathematics, December 10, 2014, retrieved 2015-01-26.</ref>
